summary: 18 Java files / ~3,080 LOC of a real, working, competition-season robot: swerve + 4-camera PhotonVision fusion + a 3-DOF shoot-on-the-move turret/rack/flywheel + ground intake + CANdle LEDs, driven by PathPlanner autos. It is genuinely team-authored (only TunerConstants.java is CTRE-generated), and the shooter math is the most sophisticated thing in the survey set: an iterative virtual-target solver compensating for robot translation, robot rotation crossed with the off-center turret offset, and indexer-imparted ball spin. Architecture is plain WPILib command-based with NO AdvantageKit, no IO layers, no simulation beyond CTRE's generated swerve sim thread, and no test sources at all. Everything is tuned by editing Constants.java (or a `static {}` block of InterpolatingDoubleTreeMaps inside ShooterSubsystem) and redeploying — SmartDashboard is used write-only, with zero getNumber/Preferences/tunable-number reads anywhere. The dominant cost centers are: five near-identical Command classes that copy-paste the same alliance-target-selection block; hand-rolled per-motor Slot0Configs/CurrentLimits/soft-limit boilerplate repeated in every subsystem; ad-hoc `degrees ÷ 360 ÷ negativeGearRatio` conversions with sign hacks; and three disagreeing sources of truth for drivetrain geometry (tuner-project.json vs TunerConstants.java vs pathplanner/settings.json). CLAUDE.md is well-written but already stale — it documents files, bindings, and versions that no longer exist.
stack: Java 17 (`sourceCompatibility = VERSION_17`, build.gradle:6-9). GradleRIO 2026.2.1. Vendordeps: Phoenix6 26.1.1, PathplannerLib 2026.1.2, photonlib v2026.2.2, WPILibNewCommands 1.0.0 (CLAUDE.md claims Phoenix 26.1.0 and PhotonVision v2026.1.1 — both stale). Hardware: 4x SDS L3 swerve modules with WCP Kraken X60 TalonFX drive+steer, CANcoders (RemoteCANcoder feedback, not FusedCANcoder — "requires Phoenix Pro"), Pigeon 2 (ID 5), all on the "rio" bus; 5 more TalonFX on the intake (IDs 20-24), 3 on the shooter/turret (25-27), 1 turret indexer (28), 1 CTRE CANdle (29) driving 7 onboard + 60 strip LEDs. 4x PhotonVision cameras (Back_Left/Back_Right/Front_Left/Front_Right). Autos: PathPlanner AutoBuilder + NamedCommands + SendableChooser, 6 autos / 20 paths in src/main/deploy/pathplanner. Logging/replay: CTRE SignalLogger (hoot) + `HootAutoReplay().withTimestampReplay().withJoystickReplay()` (Robot.java:19-21). No AdvantageKit, no Choreo. `includeDesktopSupport = true`, `wpi.sim.addGui().defaultEnabled = true`, JUnit 5 wired in build.gradle:74-81 but `src/test` does not exist.

patterns.name: Multi-camera AprilTag fusion with validation + distance-scaled std devs
patterns.whatItDoes: Bundles each PhotonCamera with its PhotonPoseEstimator, robotToCamera Transform3d and a name into a private `CameraConfig` class; iterates all of them, drains `getAllUnreadResults()` but only processes the newest frame (explicitly to avoid an overrun feedback spiral), prefers `estimateCoprocMultiTagPose` and falls back to `estimateLowestAmbiguityPose`, rejects estimates using blacklisted tag IDs, rejects ambiguity > 0.2 on single-tag, rejects poses outside field bounds +/-0.5 m, rejects avg tag distance > 6 m, then scales base std devs by `1.0 + d^2/30.0`. Results come back as a record and are pushed into the drivetrain from a default command.
patterns.libraryValue: Highest-value extraction target in the repo and already ~90% generic. The only thing binding it to 8793 is that the four cameras are hardcoded as four fields, four estimators, four `isXConnected()` methods and a 5-argument `updateVision(...)`. A library `VisionFuser` taking `List<CameraSpec{name, robotToCamera}>` plus a `RejectionPolicy` (ambiguity, max distance, field-bounds margin, ignored tag set) and a pluggable `StdDevModel` would delete ~200 lines here and make adding a camera a one-line change instead of a 4-file change.

patterns.name: Shoot-on-the-move iterative virtual-target solver
patterns.whatItDoes: Fixed-point iteration (10 passes) walking the aim point backwards along projected drift during flight. Correctly derives the *launch point's* field velocity rather than chassis velocity, adding the tangential term from robot angular rate crossed with the turret's off-center offset. Then adds indexer-spin correction decomposed into along-barrel (cos(turretAngle)) and perpendicular (sin(turretAngle)) components, both multiplied by flight time from an empirical distance->seconds table.
patterns.libraryValue: Every shooter game re-derives this and most teams get the omega-cross-r term wrong. A `MotionCompensatedAimSolver` — inputs (target Translation3d, launch pose, field-relative ChassisSpeeds, flight-time lookup), outputs (virtual target, converged flag, iterations used) — is directly liftable. The library version should add what is missing here: a convergence tolerance instead of a hardcoded 10 iterations, and a divergence guard so it cannot sit in a limit cycle.

patterns.name: Continuous-turret angle unwrapping with soft-limit wraparound
patterns.whatItDoes: Converts a desired absolute turret angle into a motor position while tracking the last commanded angle, so the turret follows smoothly across the +/-180 degree atan2 discontinuity instead of unwinding. If the unwrapped target would exceed a physical limit it wraps 360 degrees to the other side of the >360-degree travel range, then safety-clamps. Paired with soft limits derived from the same degree constants at class-init.
patterns.whereSeen: C:/Users/ericj/GitHub/8793-2026-Robot/src/main/java/frc/robot/subsystems/ShooterSubsystem.java:349-369 (angleToTurretPosition); soft limits derived at :48-71; omega feedforward at :408-415
patterns.libraryValue: This is subtle, correct, and universally needed by any turret/azimuth mechanism with more than 360 degrees of travel — and it is exactly the kind of code a team writes once at 2am and never revisits. A library `ContinuousAxis` (travel range in real units, last-setpoint memory, wrap-to-other-side policy, clamp) plus a built-in chassis-omega counter-rotation feedforward would give every future PumpkinLib turret this behavior for free and make it unit-testable off-robot.

patterns.name: Distance-indexed empirical lookup tables in a static initializer
patterns.whatItDoes: Three parallel `InterpolatingDoubleTreeMap`s — distance->rack angle (deg), distance->flywheel motor RPS, distance->time-of-flight (s) — populated in a `static {}` block with ~20 measured points each spanning 1.36 m to 15 m, with inline comments recording the physics used to extrapolate past 8 m.
patterns.libraryValue: The three tables are always keyed by the same distance and always looked up together, but nothing enforces shared breakpoints (they currently differ). A library `ShotTable` keyed by distance returning a `ShotSolution(rackAngleDeg, flywheelRps, flightTimeSec)` record — loadable from a deploy-directory CSV/JSON so it can be re-tuned at the field without recompiling — is a large practical win for any shooter game.

patterns.name: Per-subsystem lifecycle command triad: stop() / disabledCommand() / maintainStateCommand()
patterns.whatItDoes: A hand-rolled convention repeated on all three mechanism subsystems: `stop()` for command teardown, `disabledCommand()` returning `run(...).ignoringDisable(true)` bound to `RobotModeTriggers.disabled().whileTrue(...)`, and `maintainStateCommand()` registered as the default command so motor outputs are re-established after a disabled->enabled transition.
patterns.whereSeen: ShooterSubsystem.java:442-462, GroundIntakeSubsystem.java:182-209, TurretSubsystem.java:36-50; all bound in RobotContainer.java:148-157
patterns.libraryValue: Exactly the shape a library base class should own: a `PumpkinSubsystem` (or `MechanismLifecycle` mixin) supplying `neutralOnDisable()`, `holdPosition()` and `stop()` for free from a declared list of managed motors, so teams stop hand-writing three near-identical methods per subsystem. The library version must not repeat this repo's mistake of naming it `maintainState` while actually commanding zero.

patterns.name: Telemetry facade: paired NetworkTables publishers + SignalLogger writes + Mechanism2d module viz
patterns.whatItDoes: Single class owning typed NT publishers (`StructPublisher<Pose2d>`, `StructArrayPublisher<SwerveModuleState>`, `BooleanPublisher`, ...) grouped into DriveState/Pose/Vision tables, mirroring every value into `SignalLogger.writeStruct/writeDouble/writeBoolean`, plus four Mechanism2d gauges for module speed/direction. Includes real allocation-avoidance care: pre-allocated `Pose2d[][]` buckets indexed by estimate count, a reusable `double[3]` pose array, and a `HashMap<String,String[]>` caching SignalLogger key strings per camera so no strings are built in the loop.
patterns.libraryValue: Every publish site is written twice (once NT, once SignalLogger) with the key duplicated as a string literal in both — 20+ paired lines and a standing key-drift risk. A library `LogEntry`/`Publisher` that registers a key once and fans out to NT + hoot (+ optionally DataLog) would halve this file. The pre-allocation and key-caching tricks should be the library's default behavior so teams get them without knowing they needed them.

patterns.name: Drive speed-mode scaling plus normalized deadband
patterns.whatItDoes: Base max speed/angular rate captured once from `TunerConstants.kSpeedAt12Volts`, then mutable `MaxSpeed`/`MaxAngularRate` fields are rescaled by named multipliers when a mode button is pressed, via `.alongWith(Commands.runOnce(this::setShooterModeSpeeds))`. Paired with a hand-written deadband that correctly rescales the remaining range instead of leaving a discontinuity.
patterns.libraryValue: A `DriverInput` builder (deadband, expo/squaring curve, slew limiting, per-mode speed scaling, alliance-aware inversion) is the most universally copy-pasted 30 lines in FRC. The library should own it, including the correctly-normalized deadband this repo already got right.

patterns.name: Derived soft limits computed from human-readable angle constants
patterns.whatItDoes: Rather than typing motor rotations into soft-limit configs, the subsystem computes them from degree constants and the gear ratio at class-init, using Math.max/Math.min to survive a negative gear ratio flipping the direction sense. Same idea repeated for the rack.
patterns.libraryValue: The right instinct, implemented by hand three times (turret, rack, intake pivot). A library `MechanismAxis` taking {gearing with an explicit inversion flag rather than a negative ratio, min/max in real units, zero offset} and emitting soft limits, unit conversions and clamped setpoints would make the entire sign-hack class of bug unrepresentable.

patterns.name: Match-state LED controller driven by game data and match time
patterns.whatItDoes: CANdle subsystem with pre-built `SolidColor` control requests per color, a software strobe deliberately chosen over device-side StrobeAnimation so the flash cannot persist past its window, a sine brightness wave for disabled/auto, and a state machine mapping match time + game-data char + alliance to hub-active/inactive, ramping flash rate 1->8 Hz as a shift boundary approaches.
patterns.libraryValue: The game-rule half is 2026-specific and should NOT go in a library. The mechanism half should: reusable per-color control requests, a software strobe with frequency ramp, a sine brightness envelope, and index-range segmentation — this repo hardcodes `LED_END = 7 + LED_COUNT` with a comment explaining the CANdle's onboard LEDs, and a `CandleSegment` abstraction removes that magic 7 for every future team.

painPoints.problem: Five mode Command classes are ~85% identical copy-paste, and the alliance-target-selection block is duplicated verbatim in four of them
painPoints.libraryFix: An `AllianceValue<T>` / `AllianceUtil.select(blue, red)` type (defaulting to blue and caching per-enable, since `getAlliance()` is currently polled every 20 ms in four commands), plus a declarative superstructure-mode builder so a 'mode' is a data declaration (pivot setpoint, roller speed, indexer speed, aim target, delay before feeding) instead of a 60-line Command subclass.

painPoints.problem: Three disagreeing sources of truth for the same drivetrain geometry
painPoints.evidence: tuner-project.json says `DriveRatio: 6.122448979591837`, `SteerRatio: 12.8`, `CouplingRatio: 3.5714`, `VerticalTrackSizeInches: 22.5`, FL `EncoderOffset: 0.28662109375`. TunerConstants.java:92-96 says `kCoupleRatio = 5.4`, `kDriveGearRatio = 5.67`, `kSteerGearRatio = 12.1`; TunerConstants.java:143 says `kFrontLeftEncoderOffset = Rotations.of(0.15717)`; module positions are `Inches.of(10)` (a 20 in track, not 22.5 in). src/main/deploy/pathplanner/settings.json independently repeats `driveGearing: 5.67`, `robotTrackwidth: 0.508`, `flModuleX: 0.254`, `maxDriveSpeed: 5.44`. Nothing cross-checks them, and a Tuner X regeneration silently reverts hand-edits.
painPoints.libraryFix: A single `DrivetrainGeometry` record as sole source of truth, plus a startup self-check that reads `RobotConfig.fromGUISettings()` and the TunerConstants values and raises a WPILib Alert / `DriverStation.reportError` on any mismatch of gearing, wheel radius, module offsets or max speed. ~40 lines of library code that prevents a whole category of silently-wrong odometry.

painPoints.problem: `maintainStateCommand()` does not maintain state — it commands home/zero, and the RobotContainer comment claims the opposite
painPoints.evidence: RobotContainer.java:153-154 comments 'continuously re-apply current state so motor outputs are restored correctly after a disabled -> enabled transition', but ShooterSubsystem.java:456-462 is `run(() -> { setTurretRotatorPosition(0); setShooterRackPosition(0); setShooterFlywheelVelocity(0); })` and GroundIntakeSubsystem.java:204-209 is `run(() -> { pivotUp(); setRollerSpeed(0.0); })`. The moment any mode command ends or is interrupted, the default command slams the turret to 0 and the intake to the up hard stop.
painPoints.libraryFix: Library-provided `holdCurrentPositionCommand()` that latches the last commanded setpoint on first execute and re-issues it, plus a distinctly-named `homeCommand()` for the snap-to-zero behavior — so the method name can never lie about which one is bound.

painPoints.problem: Encoder seeding double-applies the gear ratio (latent bug, currently masked by a zero value)
painPoints.evidence: GroundIntakeSubsystem.java:59-60 sets `FeedbackConfigs.withSensorToMechanismRatio(PIVOT_GEAR_RATIO)`, so `getPosition()`/`setPosition()` are in mechanism rotations. But the constructor at GroundIntakeSubsystem.java:117-119 seeds with `m_leftPivotMotor.setPosition(PIVOT_UP_ROTATIONS * PIVOT_GEAR_RATIO)`. That multiplication is wrong under SensorToMechanismRatio. It is harmless only because `PIVOT_UP_ROTATIONS = 0.0` (Constants.java:178, still marked `// TODO: measure`). The instant anyone measures the real stow angle, the pivot is seeded 18x off — with kG gravity compensation reading the wrong arm angle.
painPoints.libraryFix: A `MechanismAxis.seedTo(Angle)` helper that owns the ratio and the units so callers never hand-multiply. More generally: never expose the raw rotor-vs-mechanism unit choice to team code.

painPoints.problem: Gear ratios encode direction as a negative number and are divided rather than multiplied, with a comment admitting the confusion
painPoints.evidence: Constants.java:45 `TURRET_ROTATOR_GEAR_RATIO = -20 / 200.0;` (also relies on int/double promotion to avoid integer division), Constants.java:54 `RACK_GEAR_RATIO = -1.0 / 333.33;` followed by Constants.java:57 `// Rack gear ratio is backwards`. Conversions are then `angle / 360.0 / GEAR_RATIO` in seven places (ShooterSubsystem.java:51, :54, :65, :368, :379, :413, :437), and `setTurretRotatorAngle` explicitly relies on two negatives cancelling: `// Convert rad/s -> turret rot/s -> motor rot/s (gear ratio is negative, so signs cancel)`.
painPoints.libraryFix: A `Gearing` type with a positive `reduction` plus an explicit `inverted` boolean and `toMechanism(Angle)` / `toRotor(Angle)` methods. Removes the sign-cancellation reasoning entirely and makes `-20 / 200.0` unrepresentable.

painPoints.problem: All tuning is compile-time; SmartDashboard is used write-only so nothing can be adjusted at the field
painPoints.evidence: 14 `SmartDashboard.put*` calls (ShooterSubsystem.java:327-335, GroundIntakeSubsystem.java:192-194, Telemetry.java:45) and zero `SmartDashboard.getNumber`, zero `Preferences`, zero tunable-number abstraction — grep for `Preferences|LoggedNetworkNumber|advantagekit|org.littletonrobotics` across src/main/java returns nothing. Every PID gain (Constants.java:38-64, :195-206), every shot-table point (ShooterSubsystem.java:100-168), the 0.25 s / 0.75 s feed delays and the 20-degree trench rack angle require an edit + `./gradlew deploy` to change.
painPoints.libraryFix: A `TunableDouble` that reads a compile-time default, publishes to NT under a stable key, and only accepts dashboard overrides when a `tuningMode` flag is on (so competition builds stay deterministic), plus `TunableGains` that pushes a changed Slot0Configs to the TalonFX only on change. Also: load the shot tables from `Filesystem.getDeployDirectory()` so they can be re-tuned between matches without a rebuild.

painPoints.problem: `optimizeBusUtilization()` is called on motors whose status signals are never re-enabled — a silent stale-data trap
painPoints.evidence: ShooterSubsystem.java:180, :185, :189 call `optimizeBusUtilization()` on all three shooter motors with no preceding `setUpdateFrequency`. GroundIntakeSubsystem.java:92-93 shows the author knows the correct pattern (`m_leftPivotMotor.getPosition().setUpdateFrequency(50); m_leftPivotMotor.optimizeBusUtilization();`) but it is applied in only one of eight call sites. Any future `getPosition()`/`getVelocity()` read on a shooter motor returns a frozen value with no error — and `isAtPosition`-style logic built on it would silently never be true.
painPoints.libraryFix: A motor-configuration builder where you declare which signals you consume, and it derives the `setUpdateFrequency` calls and the `optimizeBusUtilization()` call in the correct order — making it impossible to optimize away a signal you asked for.

painPoints.problem: Static initializer can hard-kill robot code with an unhelpful ExceptionInInitializerError
painPoints.evidence: Constants.java:85-87 and :93-95 run `VisionConstants.APRIL_TAG_FIELD_LAYOUT.getTagPose(26).orElseThrow()` and `.getTagPose(10).orElseThrow()` during class initialization of `ShooterConstants`. If the loaded `AprilTagFields.kDefaultField` layout ever lacks tag 26 or 10 (offseason field, layout version bump, welded-vs-andymark variant), the robot program dies at class-load with no actionable message.
painPoints.libraryFix: A `FieldConstants` accessor that resolves tag poses lazily with a named fallback and raises a persistent Alert instead of throwing, so a bad field layout degrades to 'shooter aiming disabled' rather than 'robot code does not start'.

painPoints.problem: Dead code, no-ops, and stale comments that actively mislead
painPoints.evidence: `zeroTurretEncoderOnce()` javadoc says 'account for the 15 degree rightward offset at boot' but the code is `setPosition(-0 / 360.0 / GEAR_RATIO)` (ShooterSubsystem.java:432-440) — the offset was zeroed out and the doc left behind. `PIVOT_FORCE_DOWN_POWER = 0` (Constants.java:224) makes `forceDownMode()` (GroundIntakeSubsystem.java:169-172) a no-op. `VisionSubsystem.isFrontCamera()` (:337-340) and the `m_intakeSubsystem` field are dead — their only caller is commented out at :176-180, yet RobotContainer.java:61 still constructs `new VisionSubsystem(intake)`. TurretSubsystem.java:4-7 imports Slot0Configs/PositionVoltage/StaticBrake, two unused. Stale value comments abound: `ROLLER_INTAKE_SPEED = 1; // 95% duty cycle`, `RIGHT_INDEXER_SPEED = 0.75; // 60% duty cycle`, `TURRET_INDEXER_SPEED = .65; // 60%`, `SHOOTER_MODE_MAX_SPEED_MULTIPLIER = 0.75; // 50% of max speed`, `PIVOT_GEAR_RATIO = 18.0; // 10 rotor rotations per 1 arm rotation`, `PIVOT_DOWN_ROTATIONS = 0.355; // 0.35 mechanism rot x 10:1 gear ratio`. RobotContainer.java:123-127 documents A/B/Y/X as 'shooter/trench/home/jam' while the actual bindings at :129-143 are rightBumper/B/A/X/Y.
painPoints.libraryFix: Not directly fixable by a library, but it argues for APIs self-describing enough that a magic number needs no comment (a `DutyCycle`/`Percent` type instead of `0.75 // 60%`), and for the library shipping a boot-time constants dump to the log so a wrong comment cannot hide a wrong value.

painPoints.problem: Magic numbers embedded in behavior code rather than named constants
painPoints.evidence: `applyLinearDeadband` hardcodes `double deadband = 0.1` (RobotContainer.java:97). Feed delays `m_timer.hasElapsed(0.25)` (ShooterMode.java:44) and `hasElapsed(0.75)` (TrenchMode.java:53, ShuttleMode.java:67). `m_Shooter.setShooterRackAngle(20)` (TrenchMode.java:51). Shuttle lateral offset `(robotY > tagY) ? tagY + 2.5 : tagY - 2.5` (ShuttleMode.java:63, with a comment that still says '+2 or -2'). PathPlanner gains inline: `new PPHolonomicDriveController(new PIDConstants(5.0,0.0,0.0), new PIDConstants(5.0,0.0,0.0))` (CommandSwerveDrivetrain.java:225-228). Vision field-bounds `double margin = 0.5` (VisionSubsystem.java:275) and stddev divisor `30.0` (:322). Solver iteration count `for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++)` (ShooterSubsystem.java:248). Current limits are inline literals in every subsystem (e.g. ShooterSubsystem.java:73-89 has three CurrentLimitsConfigs with 40/80, 25/35, 35/45 amps, none of which appear in Constants.java).
painPoints.libraryFix: Library defaults with named, overridable config objects (`DeadbandConfig`, `CurrentLimitProfile`, `VisionRejectionPolicy`, `AimSolverConfig`, `PathFollowingGains`) so a number has a name and a home the first time it is written.

painPoints.problem: Camera count is hardcoded into method signatures across three files, with a transposable all-boolean argument list
painPoints.evidence: VisionSubsystem has four camera fields, four estimators and four `isBackLeftConnected()`-style methods (:347-376); `Telemetry.updateVision(List, boolean, boolean, boolean, boolean)` (:165) takes one boolean per camera plus four dedicated BooleanPublisher fields (:69-72); RobotContainer.java:193 passes them as `(estimates, vision.isBackLeftConnected(), vision.isBackRightConnected(), vision.isFrontRightConnected(), vision.isFrontLeftConnected())` — four same-typed positional booleans that would swap silently.
painPoints.libraryFix: `List<CameraStatus>` / `Map<String,Boolean>` in the telemetry API with per-camera NT subtables derived from the camera name. Adding camera #5 becomes one entry in a list instead of edits to three files.

painPoints.problem: Zero simulation support for anything the team wrote — the highest-risk math is untestable off-robot
painPoints.evidence: The only sim is CTRE-generated: `startSimThread()` with a 4 ms Notifier calling `updateSimState` (CommandSwerveDrivetrain.java:41-42, :292-305). `Robot.simulationPeriodic()` is empty (Robot.java:82). Grep for `isSimulation|Sim(` outside CommandSwerveDrivetrain returns nothing — no TalonFXSimState for intake/turret/rack/flywheel, no VisionSystemSim/PhotonCameraSim, no SingleJointedArmSim/FlywheelSim. `src/test` does not exist at all. So the shoot-on-the-move solver, the turret unwrapping, the shot tables and the pivot seeding can only be validated on a real robot during a real match.
painPoints.libraryFix: Library-side simulated mechanism wrappers (arm/elevator/flywheel/turret backed by WPILib physics sims and auto-wired to TalonFXSimState) that activate on `RobotBase.isSimulation()` with no team code changes, plus a PhotonVision VisionSystemSim built from the same `CameraSpec` list used on the real robot. Keeping the pure math (aim solver, angle unwrap, gearing conversion, shot tables) HAL-free so it is unit-testable is the single highest-leverage design constraint for PumpkinLib.

painPoints.evidence: VisionSubsystem.java:58 `private final List<VisionPoseEstimate> m_estimatesBuffer = new ArrayList<>(4);` and :155-163 `m_estimatesBuffer.clear(); ...; return m_estimatesBuffer;`. RobotContainer.java:181-193 holds that list, iterates it, then hands the same reference to `logger.updateVision(estimates, ...)`. It works today only because both consumers run before the next call; any caller that retains the list gets it silently emptied 20 ms later.
painPoints.libraryFix: Push-based API (`vision.consumeEstimates(drivetrain::addVisionMeasurement)` or a registered consumer) instead of returning a recycled collection — keeps the zero-allocation benefit without exposing the aliasing hazard.

painPoints.evidence: CLAUDE.md:31-32 documents `constants/VisionConstants.java`, which does not exist (VisionConstants is a nested class inside `constants/Constants.java`); the Project Structure block omits `commands/` entirely and 4 of the 6 subsystems; CLAUDE.md:27 says '50ms loop' while `Robot extends TimedRobot` uses the default 20 ms; CLAUDE.md:53-59 documents 'A button: Brake mode (X-pattern)' and 'B button: Point wheels toward left stick', both replaced by ShooterMode/TrenchMode at RobotContainer.java:132-137 (the brake request field at :53 is now unused and the binding is commented out at :121); CLAUDE.md:72-75 lists Phoenix 26.1.0 / PhotonVision v2026.1.1 vs actual vendordeps 26.1.1 / v2026.2.2. CLAUDE.md:15-17 documents `./gradlew test` and .vscode/settings.json defines a `WPIlibUnitTests` config, but `src/test` does not exist. A 12.7 MB GIF named `Right Side Auto` is committed at the repo root. TunerConstants.java:84 still has the generator default `new CANBus("", "./logs/example.hoot")`.
painPoints.libraryFix: Out of scope for the library core, but PumpkinLib should ship a project template/archetype with constants layout, a smoke-test source set, and a task that generates the structure/bindings documentation from the code so it cannot drift by hand.

constraints: Java 17 exactly — build.gradle:6-9 pins sourceCompatibility/targetCompatibility to VERSION_17. No language features beyond 17 (records and sealed types are fine; pattern-matching switch is not).

GradleRIO 2026.2.1 with WPILib 2026 and vendordep-based resolution (build.gradle:1-3; settings.gradle resolves the frcHome maven under C:/Users/Public/wpilib/2026). PumpkinLib must ship as a vendordep JSON (or a composite/source dependency) resolvable by GradleRIO 2026, and must survive the fat-jar packaging in build.gradle:90-95.

CTRE Phoenix 6 v26.1.1 is the entire hardware layer — TalonFX, CANcoder, Pigeon 2, CANdle, Slot0Configs, MotionMagicVoltage, PositionVoltage, VelocityVoltage, Follower, NeutralOut, StaticBrake, SolidColor/RGBWColor. There is not a single REV/SparkMax device in the repo. Any hardware abstraction must be zero-cost for a pure-CTRE team and must not hide Phoenix's on-motor closed loop behind a roboRIO-side controller.

CTRE Tuner X owns src/main/java/frc/robot/generated/TunerConstants.java and can regenerate it at any time (CLAUDE.md:87: 'avoid manual edits unless updating specific values'). tuner-project.json at the repo root is likewise Tuner X's file. The library must consume TunerConstants, never require edits inside it.

The swerve drivetrain is inheritance-bound: `CommandSwerveDrivetrain extends TunerSwerveDrivetrain implements Subsystem` where `TunerSwerveDrivetrain extends SwerveDrivetrain<TalonFX,TalonFX,CANcoder>` (TunerConstants.java:219). A library drivetrain abstraction cannot supply its own base class — it must work by composition, by interface, or via the same subclass hook, and must preserve the CTRE idioms already in use: `registerTelemetry(Consumer<SwerveDriveState>)` and `applyRequest(Supplier<SwerveRequest>)`.

Vision timestamps must be translated between FPGA time and Phoenix time. CommandSwerveDrivetrain.java:314-350 overrides all three `addVisionMeasurement`/`samplePoseAt` entry points solely to wrap timestamps in `Utils.fpgaToCurrentTime(...)`. Any library vision path feeding a CTRE pose estimator must do the same or it silently corrupts the Kalman fusion.

PathPlanner 2026.1.2 is the auto framework and its call ordering is load-bearing: `NamedCommands.registerCommand(...)` must run BEFORE `AutoBuilder.configure(...)` (RobotContainer.java:70-76 has an explicit comment about this), `RobotConfig.fromGUISettings()` reads src/main/deploy/pathplanner/settings.json, `AutoBuilder.buildAutoChooser()` populates the SendableChooser, and the drive consumer must forward `feedforwards.robotRelativeForcesXNewtons()/Y` into `SwerveRequest.ApplyRobotSpeeds` (CommandSwerveDrivetrain.java:208-236).

Logging is CTRE SignalLogger/hoot, not AdvantageKit. `SignalLogger.start()` is called from the Telemetry constructor (Telemetry.java:41) and `HootAutoReplay().withTimestampReplay().withJoystickReplay()` is updated first thing in robotPeriodic (Robot.java:19-21, :29). Do not design the library around AdvantageKit's Logger/IO-layer/@AutoLog model or around a Robot base class that owns the logging lifecycle — it must coexist with hoot replay and with registerTelemetry.

`optimizeBusUtilization()` is applied to every TalonFX in the project (8 call sites). Any library code that reads status signals must explicitly `setUpdateFrequency` on the signals it needs first, or loudly document that it does not — otherwise it will read frozen values on this robot.

Stated team conventions (CLAUDE.md:61-66): `m_fieldName` private fields, `kConstantName` or UPPER_SNAKE_CASE constants, packages under `frc.robot.{subsystems, constants, commands, generated}`, and 'Use WPILib Units system for type-safe measurements'. In practice the units guidance is honored only in generated TunerConstants and RobotContainer's `.in(MetersPerSecond)`; team code is raw doubles with units baked into constant names (`_METERS`, `_ROTATIONS`, `_RPS2`, `_DEG`, `_MS`). A units-typed library API matches the stated convention but is a migration for existing code, so it needs raw-double escape hatches.

Subsystem base-class choice is inconsistent and must be tolerated: hand-written mechanisms use `implements Subsystem` (ShooterSubsystem, TurretSubsystem, GroundIntakeSubsystem, CommandSwerveDrivetrain) while VisionSubsystem and LEDSubsystem `extends SubsystemBase`. Any library base class must be optional, not mandatory.

No test infrastructure exists (`src/test` absent) despite JUnit 5 wired in build.gradle:74-81 and a WPIlibUnitTests launch config in .vscode/settings.json. The library must be useful with zero tests written, but should keep its pure-math surface (aim solver, angle unwrapping, gearing conversion, shot tables, deadband) HAL-free so it can be exercised off-robot.

Windows-only dev environment: JAVA_HOME is C:/Users/Public/wpilib/2026/jdk per .claude/settings.local.json, and .vscode/settings.json uses ${workspaceFolder}/build/jni/release. Any build scripts or codegen the library ships must work on Windows and under Git Bash.

Team 8793, project year 2026 (.wpilib/wpilib_preferences.json). All 14 TalonFX + Pigeon 2 + CANdle share the single default 'rio' CAN bus (`new CANBus("", ...)` in TunerConstants.java:84, and every device in Constants.java uses the default bus). CAN utilization is a genuine constraint — it is why optimizeBusUtilization is everywhere — so library defaults must be bus-frugal, not chatty.
